In particular, if both n and l are about log p, is it true that I = O((nl)2=3)? If n and l are both large, then the estimate in question may fail: say, for n = p2 we have I = pl, which is not bounded by (nl)2=3 + n + l if l=p ! 1. artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $\mathbb{F}_p$ denote the field with $p$ elements. For a finite set $P$ of points in $\mathbb{F}_p 	imes \mathbb{F}_p$ and a finite set $L$ of lines in $\mathbb{F}_p 	imes \mathbb{F}_p$, let $I(P,L) = |\{(q,\ell) \in P 	imes L : q \in \ell\}|$ denote the number of point-line incidences. Set $n=|P|$ and $\ell=|L|$.

It is known that one cannot have an incidence bound of Szemerédi–Trotter type valid for all sizes: e.g. taking $P = \mathbb{F}_p 	imes \mathbb{F}_p$ (so $n = p^2$) gives $I = p\ell$, which exceeds $(n\ell)^{2/3} + n + \ell$ when $\ell/p 	o \infty$.

Question: Determine a "reasonable" range of $n$ and $\ell$ (in terms of $p$) within which there is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for every prime $p$ and every choice of $P$ and $L$ with $|P|=n$ and $|L|=\ell$ in that range, one has
$$I(P,L) \le C igl((n\ell)^{2/3} + n + \ell igr).$$
In particular, prove or disprove that if $n$ and $\ell$ are both of order $\log p$, then $I(P,L) = O((n\ell)^{2/3})$.
artifact.status_search_result: Quantitative improvements over the trivial bound are known. Bourgain–Katz–Tao gave the first non-trivial improvement with a very small explicit exponent gain. Subsequent works (notably Helfgott–Rudnev, Jones, and Stevens–de Zeeuw) gave better bounds; Stevens–de Zeeuw proved $I(P,L) \lesssim |P|^{11/15}|L|^{11/15}$ under balanced-size conditions and $|P|^{-2}|L|^{13} \lesssim p^{15}$. However, the sharp Szemerédi–Trotter bound $(n\ell)^{2/3}+n+\ell$ in $\mathbb{F}_p \times \mathbb{F}_p$ (e.g. for $n,\ell \approx \log p$) remains open.

status_evidence.title: Szemerédi–Trotter theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Bourgain, Katz and Tao show that if the generic example is excluded, then an incidence bound that is an improvement on the trivial bound can be attained.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial improvements over the trivial bound are known in finite fields.

status_evidence.title: Stevens–de Zeeuw incidence bound
status_evidence.claim: Best known bound is $11/15$ exponent, weaker than the conjectured $2/3$.
